name: noetrail-synthetic-retrieval-1
about: A small retrieval set written for this repository. It is NOT an external
benchmark: the entries, the queries, and the relevance judgements were all
written by hand here, so a number measured on it says how the two ranking
modes compare on this corpus and nothing about how Noetrail compares to
another system. LoCoMo, LongMemEval and BEAM numbers are not reproducible
in this repository and none are claimed.
The judgements were fixed while writing the entries, before either ranking
mode was run over them, and the query list deliberately contains cases the
substring path wins -- a prefix of a longer word and a singular form of a
plural -- because a set that only contains cases BM25 wins measures the

entries.title: Espresso grind size notes
entries.text: Dialling in the grinder: a finer grind raises extraction and pressure. Nine bar, twenty-five seconds, eighteen grams in and thirty-six out.

entries.title: Burr grinder cleaning
entries.text: Brushed the burrs and removed the old grounds. Stale oils turn the cup bitter after about two weeks.

entries.title: Water hardness for brewing
entries.text: Soft water under-extracts and tastes flat. Aiming for around eighty parts per million total hardness.

entries.title: Cold brew ratio
entries.text: One to eight, sixteen hours in the fridge, coarse grind. Much less acidity than hot brewing.

entries.title: Bitter shots after the new bag
entries.text: The last three shots tasted bitter and hollow. Probably over-extraction from too fine a grind.

entries.title: Sourdough starter routine
entries.text: Feeds twice a day at room temperature, one to one to one. It doubles in five hours when it is healthy.

entries.title: Hydration and crumb
entries.text: Seventy-eight per cent hydration gives an open crumb, but the dough is much harder to shape.

entries.title: Oven spring problems
entries.text: Flat loaves again. Under-proofed dough and an oven that never reached temperature.

entries.title: Rye levain experiment
entries.text: Whole rye levain at twenty per cent, sour and dense. Better on the second day.

entries.title: Chain wear measurement
entries.text: The gauge dropped in at zero point seven five, so the chain is done. Replacing it early saves the cassette.

entries.title: Hydraulic brake bleed
entries.text: Bled the rear brake with mineral oil. The lever felt spongy before and the bite point is back where it should be.

entries.title: Tubeless sealant top-up
entries.text: Sealant dries out after about four months. Thirty millilitres per tyre.

entries.title: Winter bearing service
entries.text: Repacked the bottom bracket bearings after the road salt. The grease had been washed out completely.

entries.title: Why the tests got slow
entries.text: Every test built a fresh virtual environment. Caching it cut the suite from nine minutes to ninety seconds.

entries.title: Packaging without dependencies
entries.text: Standard library only. No wheels to audit and no supply chain to trust.

entries.title: Rust borrow checker notes
entries.text: Lifetimes get easier once you stop fighting them and restructure the ownership instead.

entries.title: Flaky integration test
entries.text: The failure only shows under load. A race between the writer thread and the reader thread.

entries.title: Profiling before optimising
entries.text: Measured first. The bottleneck was interpreter startup, not the algorithm.

entries.title: Kreuzberg ramen place
entries.text: Small counter, tonkotsu, a twenty minute wait on a Friday. Worth it.

entries.title: Neukoelln natural wine bar
entries.text: Orange wine list, no reservations, and loud after nine.

entries.title: Prenzlauer Berg bakery
entries.text: The best rye bread in the neighbourhood. Sold out by eleven.

entries.title: Late night noodles
entries.text: Open until three, hand pulled noodles, cash only.

entries.title: Sleep and afternoon caffeine
entries.text: Anything after two in the afternoon and I lie awake. The half-life is longer than I assumed.

entries.title: Running cadence
entries.text: Shorter steps and a higher turnover mean less knee pain after the long runs.

entries.title: Desk setup and neck pain
entries.text: The monitor was far too low. Raised it and the pain went away in a week.

entries.title: Low light lens choice
entries.text: The fast prime beats the zoom indoors. Wide open is soft but usable.

entries.title: Backup workflow for photos
entries.text: Two local copies and one offsite. Verified the restore, not just the backup.

entries.title: Colour profiles for printing
entries.text: Soft proofing changed the shadows more than expected.

entries.title: Kitchen water filter
entries.text: Replaced the filter cartridge. The water tastes noticeably better.

entries.title: Grinding the valve seats
entries.text: Old engine project. Grinding the valve seats by hand takes an evening.

entries.title: Brake pads for the car
entries.text: Ordered ceramic pads, less dust on the wheels.

entries.title: Backup for the vault
entries.text: A nightly copy to the external drive plus one offsite snapshot.

entries.title: Bitter greens salad
entries.text: Radicchio and chicory with a sweet dressing to balance the bitterness.

entries.title: Hard water in the kettle
entries.text: Descaled the kettle again. Limescale builds up within a month here.

queries.note: Three words that never occur together as a phrase.
The car entry about grinding valve seats is the distractor.
Two unrelated entries also mention hard water.
Four terms, two of which are on other sourdough entries.
The car brake-pad entry shares the strongest single word.
A second testing entry is the distractor.
Present as a title, so the substring path can also find it.
Term and tag, never adjacent; the substring path finds nothing.
Two genuinely relevant entries in different areas.
One word, two topics; a third entry mentions it in passing.
One rare word; both modes should find it.
A prefix of a word. The substring path wins; BM25 cannot match it.
Singular of a plural in the text. The substring path wins; BM25 has no stemmer.
A second entry is about a different kind of pain.
